latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Loss of CD4 T-cell, IFN-gamma, macrophage, and transplant immune surveillance that permits latent tissue cyst reactivation or severe primary toxoplasmosis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Tissue cyst reactivation or primary inoculation
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Conversion of latent bradyzoite cysts or newly acquired organisms into clinically active infection; the route is context dependent and should not be encoded in the disease id.
Actively replicating tachyzoite burden in blood and tissue; reduced by anti-toxoplasma folate-pathway therapy and responsible for tissue invasion.

Bloodstream spread of active Toxoplasma to CNS, lung, myocardium, retina, marrow, liver, and other tissues; disseminated presentation is a disease expression, not a separate first-layer disease name here.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Toxoplasma CNS encephalitis and abscess activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Necrotizing encephalitis with ring-enhancing lesions, edema, focal deficits, seizures, altered mental status, coma, and risk of mass effect.
Diffuse or nodular pulmonary toxoplasmosis causing cough, tachypnea, miliary or nodular infiltrates, cavitation, consolidation, hypoxemia, ARDS, and sepsis-like deterioration.
Myocardial tissue invasion and inflammatory injury producing troponin elevation, arrhythmia, reduced ejection fraction, acute heart failure, cardiogenic or mixed shock, and death.
Retinal and choroidal inflammatory necrosis causing floaters, blurred vision, photophobia, focal retinochoroiditis, vitritis, and vision-threatening lesions.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Systemic inflammatory, marrow, and HLH-like activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Cytokine activation, marrow suppression or hemophagocytosis, hepatitis, ferritin/LDH rise, cytopenias, and shock-like organ dysfunction triggered by active toxoplasmosis.
Maternal tachyzoite infection crossing the placenta and producing fetal or congenital toxoplasmosis; this is represented as a context path inside toxoplasmosis rather than renaming the disease leaf.

supportive_care: Keep Toxoplasma PCR, serology, tissue biopsy, immunohistochemistry, BAL PCR, CSF PCR, and autopsy findings as confirmatory or microbiology/pathology context rather than ordinary presentation observations in ranking cases.
For suspected CNS disease, record neurologic symptoms, focal deficits, seizures, mental status, MRI/CT lesion count and location, edema, mass effect, and CSF profile when lumbar puncture is safe.

For pulmonary presentations, track respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, imaging infiltrate/nodule extent, ventilatory support, BAL sampling, and competing opportunistic infections such as PJP, TB, CMV, cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis, and bacterial pneumonia.
For cardiac presentations, trend ECG, telemetry, echocardiography, ejection fraction, troponin, BNP/NT-proBNP when available, lactate, shock physiology, renal function, and volume status.

Assess host susceptibility explicitly: HIV status and CD4 count, ART history, HSCT or cord blood transplant timing, GVHD therapy, solid organ transplant status, tacrolimus/sirolimus/MMF/steroid exposure, malignancy, chemotherapy, and TMP-SMX prophylaxis interruption.
Monitor pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin and TMP-SMX toxicity: CBC with differential, platelets, creatinine, potassium, liver enzymes, rash, GI intolerance, and adherence.
Coordinate immunosuppression reduction with transplant, hematology, or rheumatology teams because improved parasite control can be offset by GVHD, rejection, or underlying disease flare.
In HIV-associated disease, coordinate ART timing, IRIS monitoring, secondary prophylaxis, and discontinuation only after immune recovery and clinical/radiographic stability.
In pregnancy context, involve maternal-fetal medicine and infectious diseases; model fetal hazard as a context/event path rather than changing the disease id.
Use ICU organ support when needed for hypoxemic respiratory failure, shock, cardiogenic failure, renal replacement therapy, seizures, intracranial hypertension, or multiorgan failure.
